note.explanation: A computer network connects devices so they can communicate and share resources. Data travels according to protocols; devices such as routers and switches help move it, while security tools help protect it.
examples: A school network can let many computers use one printer.
DNS finds the IP address linked to a website name.
note.checkAnswer: A router directs data packets between networks.
note.simple: A network is a group of connected devices that can exchange data and share things such as files or printers.
note.checkQuestion: Which device directs data packets between different networks?
note.title: Computer Networks: Unit Review
steps: Connect devices using a suitable network medium and devices.
Use protocols to organise and deliver data.
Use network services such as DNS and DHCP where needed.
Protect the network with tools such as firewalls and encryption.
note.answer: A computer network connects devices for data communication and resource sharing.

options: Enable resource sharing and data communication
mcqs.stem: Q6.1. What is the primary objective of computer networks?
rationales: This can sometimes be a benefit, but it is not the primary objective stated here.
This is correct: networks enable resource sharing and data communication.
Networks do not primarily exist to improve graphics.
Software development is not the primary objective of networks.

mcqs.stem: Q6.2. Which device is used to connect multiple networks and direct data packets between them?
rationales: A switch mainly connects devices within a network.
A hub sends incoming data to all connected devices and does not route between networks.
This is correct: a router connects networks and directs packets between them.
A modem connects a network to an internet service over a communication line; packet routing is the router's function.

mcqs.stem: Q6.3. Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for node-to-node data transfer and error detection?
rationales: The Physical Layer transmits raw bits over a medium.
This is correct: the Data Link Layer handles node-to-node transfer and error detection.
The Network Layer is concerned with logical addressing and routing between networks.
The Transport Layer provides end-to-end transport services.

options: Translate domain names to IP addresses
mcqs.stem: Q6.4. What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
rationales: DHCP, rather than DNS, commonly assigns IP addresses dynamically.
This is correct: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
Encryption and security protocols are used to secure communication.
Firewalls and monitoring tools can monitor network traffic.

mcqs.stem: Q6.5. Which method of data transmission uses a dedicated communication path?
rationales: Packet switching sends packets over shared routes rather than reserving one dedicated path.
This is correct: circuit switching establishes a dedicated communication path.
Full-duplex describes two-way transmission at the same time, not a switching method.
Half-duplex describes two-way transmission at different times, not a switching method.

options: Converting data into a secure format
Translating domain names to IP addresses
mcqs.stem: Q6.6. What is encapsulation in the context of network communication?
rationales: Encryption converts data into a protected form; this is not the definition of encapsulation.
This is correct: encapsulation wraps data with protocol information.
Monitoring traffic is a security or administration task, not encapsulation.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

mcqs.stem: Q6.7. Which protocol is used for reliable data transfer in the TCP/IP model?
rationales: HTTP is an application protocol and commonly relies on TCP for reliable delivery.
FTP is an application protocol for file transfer and commonly relies on TCP.
This is correct: TCP provides reliable data transfer.
UDP does not provide TCP-style guaranteed reliable delivery.

options: Convert data into a secure format
mcqs.stem: Q6.8. What is the main purpose of a firewall in network security?
rationales: Encryption converts data into a protected format; it is not a firewall's main purpose.
This is correct: a firewall monitors and controls network traffic according to rules.
DHCP is commonly used to assign IP addresses.
DNS translates domain names to IP addresses.

mcqs.stem: Q6.9. Which network topology connects all devices to a central hub?
rationales: In a ring topology, devices are connected in a closed loop.
A mesh topology provides multiple connections among devices.
In a bus topology, devices share a main backbone cable.
This is correct: a star topology connects devices to a central hub or switch.

options: Enable resource sharing and efficient communication
mcqs.stem: Q6.10. What is a key benefit of using computer networks in businesses?
rationales: This may be a possible effect in some settings, but it is not the key benefit listed.
This is correct: networks enable resource sharing and efficient communication in businesses.
Networks do not primarily enhance graphic capabilities.
Networks do not primarily improve software development.

written.text: Q6.1. Define data communication and list its key components.
written.finalAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium. Its key components are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol.

rubric.why: The definition shows what data communication means.
rubric.how: State that devices exchange data through a transmission medium.

rubric.why: The question also asks for the key components.
rubric.how: Name sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
Its key components are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol.

written.text: Q6.2. Explain the role of routers in a computer network.
written.finalAnswer: Routers connect different networks and direct data packets to their destination using suitable routes.

rubric.why: Connecting networks is a main role of a router.
rubric.how: Explain that routers connect different networks.

rubric.why: Routers must forward packets towards their destination.
rubric.how: State that routers select routes and direct data packets to destinations.

modelAnswer: Routers connect different networks.
They direct data packets to their destination using suitable routes.

written.text: Q6.3. What are the main functions of the Network Layer in the OSI model?
written.finalAnswer: The Network Layer provides logical addressing and routing, forwarding packets between networks towards their destination.

rubric.why: Logical addressing identifies devices across networks.
rubric.how: Mention logical or IP addressing.

rubric.why: Routing helps packets reach destinations across networks.
rubric.how: Explain that the layer routes or forwards packets towards their destinations.

modelAnswer: The Network Layer provides logical addressing.
It routes and forwards packets between networks towards their destination.

written.text: Q6.4. Describe the difference between packet switching and circuit switching.
written.finalAnswer: Packet switching divides data into packets that may travel over shared routes. Circuit switching establishes a dedicated communication path for the duration of the communication.

rubric.why: Packet switching is distinguished by dividing data into packets and using shared routes.
rubric.how: State that data is split into packets and sent over shared routes.

rubric.why: A dedicated path is the defining contrast for circuit switching.
rubric.how: State that it establishes a dedicated path for the communication.

modelAnswer: Packet switching divides data into packets that may travel over shared routes.
Circuit switching establishes a dedicated communication path for the duration of the communication.

written.text: Q6.5. What is the purpose of the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)?
written.finalAnswer: DHCP automatically assigns IP configuration, including IP addresses, to devices on a network.

rubric.why: DHCP provides automatic configuration rather than requiring each address to be set manually.
rubric.description: State that the process is automatic.
rubric.how: Explain that DHCP automatically assigns configuration to devices.

rubric.why: IP addresses are the key network settings asked about here.
rubric.how: Mention that DHCP assigns IP addresses.

modelAnswer: DHCP automatically assigns network configuration to devices.
This includes assigning IP addresses.

written.text: Q6.6. How does encapsulation ensure secure communication in a network?
written.finalAnswer: Encapsulation wraps data with protocol information, such as headers. It helps organise and deliver data, but by itself it does not encrypt data or guarantee security.

rubric.why: This states what encapsulation does during communication.
rubric.how: Say that it wraps data with protocol information such as headers.

rubric.why: Encapsulation alone is not encryption; distinguishing these prevents a misleading security claim.
rubric.how: Explain that encapsulation alone does not encrypt data or guarantee security.

modelAnswer: Encapsulation wraps data with protocol information, such as headers, to organise and deliver it.
By itself, encapsulation does not encrypt data or guarantee secure communication.

written.text: Q6.7. Differentiate between TCP and UDP in terms of data transfer reliability.
written.finalAnswer: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery and checks for lost data, retransmitting when needed. UDP is faster and has less overhead, but does not guarantee delivery or order.

rubric.why: TCP is the reliable-transfer protocol in this comparison.
rubric.how: State that TCP checks delivery and can retransmit lost data.

rubric.why: The key difference is that UDP does not guarantee delivery or order.
rubric.how: State that UDP has no guarantee of delivery or order.

modelAnswer: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery and retransmits data if needed.
UDP has less overhead but does not guarantee delivery or order.

written.text: Q6.8. Explain the importance of encryption in network security.
written.finalAnswer: Encryption changes readable data into an encoded form so unauthorised people cannot easily understand it. The intended recipient can decrypt it with the appropriate key.

rubric.why: Encryption protects the confidentiality of data from unauthorised access.
rubric.how: State that it converts readable data into an encoded form.

rubric.why: Decryption by the intended recipient completes the explanation of protected communication.
rubric.how: Mention that the intended recipient uses the appropriate key to decrypt data.

modelAnswer: Encryption changes readable data into an encoded form that unauthorised people cannot easily understand.
The intended recipient can decrypt it with the appropriate key.

written.text: Q6.9. What are the advantages of using a star topology in a network?
written.finalAnswer: A star topology is easy to install and manage. Failure of one device or its link usually does not affect the other devices, and faults are easier to identify.

rubric.why: Ease of installation and management is an advantage of star topology.
rubric.how: Mention that the topology is easy to install or manage.

rubric.why: Independent links help limit faults and make troubleshooting easier.
rubric.how: Explain that one device/link failure usually does not stop the others, or that faults are easier to locate.

modelAnswer: A star topology is easy to install and manage.
Failure of one device or its link usually does not affect the other devices, and faults are easier to identify.

written.text: Q6.10. How do firewalls contribute to network security?
written.finalAnswer: Firewalls monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic according to security rules, helping block unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Monitoring and controlling traffic is the firewall's central function.
rubric.how: Say that firewalls monitor and control network traffic.

rubric.why: This explains how traffic control improves security.
rubric.how: Mention that rules help prevent unauthorised access.

modelAnswer: Firewalls monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic according to security rules.
They help block unauthorised access.

written.text: Q6.1. Discuss the objectives of computer networks and provide examples of how they facilitate resource sharing and data communication.
written.finalAnswer: Computer networks enable resource sharing and data communication. They let users share hardware, software, files, and services and exchange messages or other data efficiently.

rubric.why: These are the central objectives of computer networks.
rubric.how: Identify resource sharing and data communication.

rubric.why: Concrete shared-resource examples show how the objective is achieved.
rubric.how: Explain that users can share devices such as printers and files or software.

rubric.why: Examples of data exchange demonstrate communication between networked devices.
rubric.how: Describe exchanging messages, email, or other data between devices.

rubric.why: The discussion should explain the practical value of networking.
rubric.how: Link sharing and communication to efficiency, lower duplication, or collaboration.

modelAnswer: The primary objectives of computer networks are resource sharing and data communication.
A network allows several users to share hardware, such as a printer, rather than each user needing a separate printer.
Users can also share files, software, storage, and other network services.
For example, a worker can save a file on a shared server so colleagues can access it.
Networked devices can exchange messages, email, and other data.
This makes communication faster and supports collaboration between users in different locations.
Sharing resources can reduce cost and avoid unnecessary duplication.
Thus, networks make communication and the use of resources more efficient.

written.text: Q6.2. In a Simplex communication system, assume data is transmitted at a rate of 500 bits per second (bps). Compute the time to transmit a message if: (a) it is of 10 kilobits. (b) it is of 10 kilobytes.

rubric.why: Using time equals data size divided by transmission rate sets up both calculations correctly.
rubric.description: Write the relation and convert units.
rubric.how: Use time = number of bits ÷ 500 bps and express each message size in bits.

rubric.why: The 10-kilobit result depends on using the correct bit count and rate.
rubric.how: Convert 10 kilobits to 10,000 bits and divide by 500.

rubric.why: Kilobytes must first be converted to bytes and then to bits.
rubric.how: Use 10 × 1024 bytes and 8 bits per byte.

rubric.why: The final calculation must give the correct time for part (b).
rubric.how: Divide 81,920 bits by 500 bps and state seconds.

modelAnswer: Time = Number of bits ÷ Transmission rate
(a) 10 kilobits = 10 × 1000 = 10,000 bits
Time = 10,000 ÷ 500 = 20 seconds
(b) 10 kilobytes = 10 × 1024 = 10,240 bytes

written.text: Q6.3. Describe how data is transmitted across computer networks using packet switching and circuit switching.
written.finalAnswer: Packet switching divides a message into packets that are sent over shared network routes and reassembled at the destination. Circuit switching first establishes a dedicated path that remains reserved for the communication.

rubric.why: Splitting a message into packets is the starting point of packet switching.
rubric.how: State that the message is divided into packets.

rubric.why: Routing and reassembly complete the packet-switching process.
rubric.how: Describe packets using shared routes and being reassembled at the destination.

rubric.why: A dedicated path is the defining feature of circuit switching.
rubric.how: State that a dedicated communication path is set up before transmission.

rubric.why: Explaining how the path is used distinguishes circuit switching from packet switching.
rubric.how: Explain that the path stays reserved for the communication and contrast it with shared packet routes.

modelAnswer: In packet switching, the message is divided into smaller units called packets.
Each packet carries information needed for delivery and may travel through shared network routes.
Packets can take different routes to the destination.
At the destination, the packets are put back together to form the original message.
In circuit switching, a dedicated communication path is established before data is sent.
The path remains reserved for the communication while it is in use.
Packet switching shares network capacity among packets, while circuit switching reserves a path.
Thus, the two methods differ in whether data uses shared routes or a dedicated connection.

written.text: Q6.4. Discuss the role and importance of protocols in data communication. Explain the functions of key protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP, DNS, and DHCP.
written.finalAnswer: Protocols are agreed rules that allow devices to communicate correctly. TCP/IP supports addressing and delivery across networks; HTTP transfers web information; DNS translates domain names to IP addresses; DHCP automatically assigns IP configuration.

rubric.why: Protocols make communication between different devices orderly and compatible.
rubric.how: Define protocols as agreed rules for data communication and state why they matter.

rubric.why: TCP/IP is the basic protocol suite for communication across networks.
rubric.how: Describe its role in addressing and transferring data across networks.

rubric.why: HTTP is the protocol associated with web communication.
rubric.how: State that HTTP is used to transfer web pages or web information.

rubric.why: DNS and DHCP provide distinct, important network services.
rubric.how: State that DNS maps domain names to IP addresses and DHCP assigns IP configuration automatically.

modelAnswer: A protocol is a set of agreed rules for communication between devices.
Protocols specify how data is formatted, transmitted, received, and interpreted.
TCP/IP is the main protocol suite used to communicate across interconnected networks.
IP provides addressing and routing, while TCP supports reliable data transfer.
HTTP is used to transfer web pages and other web information between a browser and a web server.
DNS translates a human-readable domain name into its corresponding IP address.
DHCP automatically provides devices with IP addresses and other network configuration.
Together, these protocols allow devices and network services to communicate in an organised way.

written.text: Q6.5. Evaluate different methods of network security, including firewalls, encryption, and antivirus software.
written.finalAnswer: Firewalls control network traffic and help block unauthorised access; encryption protects data by making it unreadable without the appropriate key; antivirus software detects and removes malicious software. They are useful together, but each has limits and should be kept updated.

rubric.why: Firewalls protect a network by filtering traffic according to rules.
rubric.how: Explain that firewalls monitor/control traffic and help block unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Encryption protects the confidentiality of transmitted or stored data.
rubric.how: Explain that encryption encodes data so it requires the correct key to read.

rubric.why: Antivirus software addresses malicious programs on devices.
rubric.how: Explain that antivirus detects, blocks, or removes malicious software.

rubric.why: Evaluation includes recognising that protections work best together and have limits.
rubric.how: State that the methods address different threats and should be maintained/updated.

modelAnswer: A firewall monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic according to security rules.
It can help block unauthorised access, but it does not by itself protect against every threat.
Encryption changes readable data into an encoded form that cannot readily be understood without the correct key.
It helps protect the confidentiality of data, especially when data is transmitted or stored.
Antivirus software detects, blocks, and removes viruses and other malicious software.
It helps protect individual devices, but it must be kept updated to recognise new threats.
These methods protect different parts of a network and work best when used together.
Regular updates and careful security practices are also needed because no single method gives complete protection.

written.text: Q6.6. Describe real-world applications of computer networks in business, education, and healthcare.
written.finalAnswer: Businesses use networks for communication and sharing files, printers, and services; education uses them for learning platforms and sharing resources; healthcare uses them to access patient information and support communication between healthcare staff.

rubric.why: Business examples should show how networks support work and resource sharing.
rubric.how: Describe business communication or sharing files, printers, or services.

rubric.why: Education applications show how networks support teaching and learning.
rubric.how: Mention online learning, educational resources, or communication between teachers and students.

rubric.why: Healthcare examples show the use of networks in care and information access.
rubric.how: Describe sharing/accessing patient information or communication between healthcare staff.

rubric.why: The response should explain the value of these applications, not just list settings.
rubric.how: Link network use to faster access, communication, or coordinated work.

modelAnswer: In business, networks let employees communicate, share files, use shared printers, and access common services.
They support collaboration between workers in different offices or locations.
In education, networks give students and teachers access to online learning platforms and digital resources.
They also support communication and sharing of assignments and learning materials.
In healthcare, networks allow authorised staff to access and share patient information, such as electronic medical records.
They can support communication between departments and healthcare providers.
These applications make information easier to access and help people coordinate their work.
Appropriate security is important, especially when sensitive business or patient data is shared.

written.text: Q6.7. Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
written.finalAnswer: Star connects each device to a central hub or switch; ring connects devices in a closed loop; bus connects devices to a shared backbone; mesh connects devices through multiple links. Their cost, reliability, and ease of troubleshooting differ.

rubric.why: The central device defines star topology.
rubric.how: State that devices connect to a central hub or switch.

rubric.why: Ring and bus have distinct connection arrangements.
rubric.how: Explain that ring forms a loop and bus uses a shared backbone.

rubric.why: Multiple paths distinguish mesh from the other topologies.
rubric.how: State that devices have multiple interconnections or paths.

rubric.why: Comparison requires considering practical strengths and limitations.
rubric.how: Compare reliability, cost, or fault isolation across the topologies.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, each device connects to a central hub or switch.
It is easy to manage, and one device or link failing usually does not stop the other devices, but the central device is a critical point.
In a ring topology, each device connects to two neighbouring devices to form a closed loop.
A break in the ring can disrupt communication unless a bypass or other protection is available.
In a bus topology, all devices share one main backbone cable.
It uses less cable, but a failure of the backbone can affect the whole network and faults may be harder to locate.
In a mesh topology, devices have multiple links or paths between them.
Mesh can be highly reliable because data may use another path, but it can require more connections and cost more.
Therefore, the topologies differ in arrangement, cost, reliability, and ease of maintenance.

written.text: Q6.8. Consider a shift cipher with a shift amount of 4. (a) Encrypt the message "SECURITY". (b) Decrypt the message "WMXYVMI".

rubric.why: The shift direction and amount must be established before transforming letters.
rubric.how: Use a forward shift of four for encryption and a backward shift of four for decryption.

rubric.why: Each letter in SECURITY must be shifted forward correctly.
rubric.how: Shift each letter of SECURITY four places forward.

rubric.why: Decryption reverses the encryption shift.
rubric.how: Shift each ciphertext letter four places backward.

rubric.why: The final decrypted text must match the given ciphertext letter by letter.
rubric.how: Write the resulting plaintext as SITURIE.

modelAnswer: Use the alphabet cyclically, shifting each letter four places forward to encrypt and four places backward to decrypt.
(a) S → W, E → I, C → G, U → Y, R → V, I → M, T → X, Y → C
Encrypted message = WIGYVMXC
(b) W → S, M → I, X → T, Y → U, V → R, M → I, I → E
Decrypted message = SITURIE

written.text: Q6.9. An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number. Calculate the total number of unique IPv4 addresses possible. (a) Show the calculation for the total number of IPv4 addresses. (b) How many addresses are left if 10% of the total addresses are reserved for special purposes?

rubric.why: Each of the 32 bits has two possible values, so the total is a power of two.
rubric.how: Show that the number of addresses is 2^32.

rubric.why: The power must be evaluated correctly.
The reserved share must be calculated from the total.
rubric.description: Calculate the reserved share or remaining percentage.
rubric.how: Recognise that 90% remains, or calculate 10% reserved.

rubric.why: The final result must state the amount remaining after the reservation.
rubric.how: Multiply the total by 0.90 and state the result, noting the approximate whole-address count.

modelAnswer: (a) Each of the 32 bits can be 0 or 1.
Total number of unique IPv4 addresses = 2^32
(b) Percentage left = 100% − 10% = 90%
Addresses left = 90% of 4,294,967,296
Approximately 3,865,470,566 whole addresses remain.

examTips: Section A tests precise terms, devices, protocols, OSI layers, and topology features; learn the distinguishing function of each term.
Short questions usually earn marks for a clear definition plus the requested components, difference, purpose, or example. Write both sides of a comparison.
For long answers, organise the response into labelled points and give examples; do not merely list terms when asked to discuss or evaluate.
For transmission-time calculations, convert the complete message size to bits before dividing by bits per second, and include the time unit.
For cipher questions, show the direction and amount of the shift, then show the resulting letters.
For IPv4, show why 32 bits give 2^32 combinations, then show the percentage calculation.

Convert 10 kilobits to bits, then divide by 500 bps.

yourTurn.answer: It is easy to install and manage; one device or link failure usually does not affect the others, and faults are easier to identify.

steps.why: The number of bits is needed because the transmission rate is measured in bits per second.
Time is the amount of data divided by the rate at which it is sent.
steps.text: Time = Number of bits ÷ Transmission rate

steps.why: Dividing bits by bits per second gives the time in seconds.
A kilobyte is converted to bytes, then each byte is converted to 8 bits.
This converts the whole message into the unit used by the transmission rate.
Dividing by the transmission rate gives the required time.

explain.title: Why networks are used
explain.body: Computer networks connect devices so they can communicate and share resources such as printers, files, software, and services.

explain.title: Data travels by rules
explain.body: Protocols are agreed rules for communication. TCP/IP supports communication across networks; HTTP transfers web information; DNS maps domain names to IP addresses; DHCP assigns IP configuration automatically.

explain.title: Moving data and choosing a layout
explain.body: Packet switching splits data into packets that may use shared routes. Circuit switching establishes a dedicated path. Star, ring, bus, and mesh describe different ways devices are connected.

explain.title: Protecting a network
explain.body: Firewalls monitor and control traffic, encryption makes data unreadable without the right key, and antivirus software helps detect malicious programs. These methods work best together.

explain.title: Show your working
explain.body: For a transmission-time problem, convert the data to bits and divide by bits per second. For a 32-bit address, count all combinations using 2^32.

mistakes: Do not confuse a router, which directs packets between networks, with a switch or hub.
Do not say that encapsulation itself encrypts data; it wraps data with protocol information.
Do not describe UDP as guaranteeing reliable delivery; TCP is the reliable protocol in this comparison.
For transmission time, do not divide kilobytes directly by a rate in bits per second; convert to bits first.
In a shift cipher, use opposite directions for encryption and decryption and apply the same shift amount.
Do not confuse 10% reserved with 10% remaining; the remaining share is 90%.
